Inventions are directed to components, subassemblies, systems, and/or methods for continuously variable transmissions (CVT). In one aspect, a control system is adapted to facilitate a change in the ratio of a CVT. A control system includes a control reference nut coupled to a feedback cam and operably coupled to a skew cam. In some cases, the skew cam is configured to interact with carrier plates of a CVT. Various inventive feedback cams and skew cams can be used to facilitate shifting the ratio of a CVT. In some transmissions described, the planet subassemblies include legs configured to cooperate with the carrier plates. In some cases, a neutralizer assembly is operably coupled to the carrier plates. A shift cam and a traction sun are adapted to cooperate with other components of the CVT to support operation and/or functionality of the CVT. Among other things, shift control interfaces for a CVT are described.

outputs.L1: The inventions are directed to components, subassemblies, systems, and/or methods for continuously variable transmissions (CVTs). In one aspect, a control system is adapted to facilitate a change in the ratio of a CVT. The control system includes a control reference nut coupled to a feedback cam and operably coupled to a skew cam. In some cases, the skew cam is configured to interact with carrier plates of a CVT. Various inventive feedback cams and skew cams may be used to facilitate shifting the ratio of a CVT. In certain transmissions described herein, the planet subassemblies include legs configured to cooperate with the carrier plates. In some cases, a neutralizer assembly is operably coupled to the carrier plates. A shift cam and a traction sun are adapted to cooperate with other components of the CVT to support operation and/or functionality of the CVT. Among other things, shift control interfaces for a CVT are described.
outputs.L2: The inventions relate to parts, subassemblies, systems, and methods associated with continuously variable transmissions (CVTs). In one implementation, a control arrangement is designed to help adjust the transmission ratio of a CVT. The control arrangement has a control reference nut connected to a feedback cam and functionally linked to a skew cam. In certain examples, the skew cam is arranged to engage with carrier plates in the CVT. Different forms of feedback cams and skew cams may be employed to assist in changing the CVT ratio. In some of the transmissions discussed, the planet subassemblies have legs designed to work together with the carrier plates. In certain instances, a neutralizer assembly is functionally connected to the carrier plates. A shift cam and a traction sun are configured to cooperate with additional CVT components to enable and/or improve CVT operation and functionality. The disclosure also includes, among other features, shift-control interfaces for a CVT.
outputs.L3:
The inventions described relate generally to components, subassemblies, systems, and methods for use in continuously variable transmissions (CVTs). These inventions may be applied to improve the operation, control, and functionality of a CVT, particularly in connection with changing or managing the transmission ratio during operation.

In one aspect, a control system is provided to facilitate changes in the transmission ratio of a CVT. The control system may be configured to receive, transmit, or generate mechanical inputs that influence the positioning of transmission components responsible for ratio adjustment. By coordinating these components, the control system can help produce controlled and responsive changes in the CVT ratio.

The control system may include a control reference nut that is coupled to a feedback cam. The control reference nut may also be operably coupled to a skew cam, allowing movement or positioning of the control reference nut to influence the skew cam and associated transmission elements. Through this arrangement, the feedback cam and skew cam can cooperate to provide feedback and control functions that assist in managing ratio changes.

In certain embodiments, the feedback cams and skew cams are configured to interact with carrier plates. This interaction may help shift the ratio of the CVT by changing the orientation, position, or operating relationship of one or more transmission elements supported by or associated with the carrier plates. As the cams engage or influence the carrier plates, they may assist in producing the desired adjustment in transmission ratio in a controlled manner.

Additional components may also be incorporated to support CVT operation and functionality. For example, planet subassembly legs may be used as part of a planet subassembly structure within the transmission. A neutralizer assembly may be provided to assist with neutral positioning, balancing, or disengagement functions. A shift cam may be included to contribute to ratio-changing operations, and a traction sun may be used to support torque transfer or traction-based operation within the CVT. Together, these components and subassemblies may cooperate to provide a continuously variable transmission with improved control, shifting behavior, and operational performance.
outputs.L4:
The inventions relate to continuously variable transmissions (CVTs) and to mechanical arrangements, subassemblies, control systems, and operating methods used to vary the transmission ratio during operation. In particular, the described technology focuses on CVT architectures that use coordinated mechanical control elements to manage shifting, regulate component positions, and improve the transfer of torque through the transmission.

A central aspect of the inventions is the use of control and feedback mechanisms that allow the CVT ratio to be adjusted in a controlled and repeatable manner. These mechanisms may include a control reference nut, a feedback cam, a skew cam, carrier plates, and shift control interfaces. Together, these elements help determine the position and movement of internal transmission components so that the effective ratio of the CVT can be changed smoothly. The control reference nut may provide a mechanical reference or adjustment point for ratio control. The feedback cam may communicate positional or operational feedback within the transmission so that the shifting system can respond appropriately. The skew cam may influence the angular or skewed orientation of certain transmission elements, thereby affecting how the CVT transitions between ratios.

The inventions also describe various subassemblies that support the operation of the transmission. These may include planet subassemblies having legs or support structures that help position rolling or traction elements within the CVT. Carrier plates may be used to support and coordinate the movement of multiple internal components. Neutralizer assemblies may assist in balancing forces, reducing unwanted movement, or helping return certain mechanisms to a neutral or controlled condition. Shift cams and shift control interfaces may provide the mechanical input needed to initiate or regulate ratio changes, either directly from an actuator or through an intermediate control linkage.

Another important feature involves traction components, such as traction suns, that participate in the transfer of torque through the CVT. These components may interact with planets, rollers, discs, or other traction elements to transmit power while allowing the transmission ratio to vary continuously rather than in fixed steps. By controlling the position, angle, or loading of these traction elements, the transmission can achieve different speed ratios between an input and an output.

Overall, the inventions provide a set of coordinated mechanical features designed to improve the shifting behavior, controllability, and functionality of continuously variable transmissions. The combination of planet subassembly legs, neutralizer assemblies, shift cams, traction suns, carrier plates, feedback cams, skew cams, and shift control interfaces supports precise ratio adjustment and reliable CVT operation. These improvements may contribute to smoother shifting, better mechanical coordination, enhanced control response, and more effective operation of the transmission across a range of speeds and torque conditions.
outputs.L5:
## Inventions and CVT: Various Innovations That Changed Motion

Throughout history, inventions have shaped the way people live, work, and travel. From simple tools to advanced machines, human creativity has led to various technological breakthroughs. One important example in the world of transportation and engineering is the CVT, or Continuously Variable Transmission.

A CVT is a type of transmission used in various vehicles, including cars, scooters, and some industrial machines. Unlike traditional transmissions that shift between fixed gears, a CVT can change smoothly through a continuous range of gear ratios. This invention allows engines to operate more efficiently, often improving fuel economy and providing a smoother driving experience.

The idea behind CVT technology is not entirely new. Early concepts of continuously variable transmission systems appeared centuries ago, and various inventors contributed to their development over time. Modern CVTs use advanced belts, pulleys, sensors, and computer controls to deliver reliable performance. These improvements have made CVTs popular in many modern vehicles.

Inventions like the CVT show how various ideas can evolve into practical solutions. A small mechanical concept can become an important part of everyday life when it is refined through engineering and innovation. Whether in transportation, manufacturing, or energy systems, inventions continue to push technology forward.

Today, the CVT remains a strong example of how various inventions can improve efficiency, comfort, and performance. As technology advances, new versions of CVT systems may become even more durable, intelligent, and environmentally friendly. This demonstrates the continuing importance of innovation in solving modern challenges.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an invention involving control systems and shift mechanisms for continuously variable transmissions (CVTs), including feedback cams, skew cams, carrier plates, and planet subassemblies.
counterfactuals.output: A control and shift mechanism for a continuously variable transmission (CVT) is provided. The mechanism includes a carrier plate supporting a plurality of planet subassemblies arranged for coordinated tilting or skewing to vary a transmission ratio between input and output members. A feedback cam is operatively coupled to a shift actuator and configured to provide positional feedback corresponding to the angular or radial displacement of the planet subassemblies. A skew cam cooperates with the feedback cam and with associated cam followers, links, or guide features to translate an actuator input into controlled skew motion of the planet subassemblies relative to the carrier plate. The feedback cam may be shaped to define a desired ratio-control profile and to compensate for nonlinear transmission characteristics, thereby improving shift accuracy, stability, and repeatability. In certain embodiments, the carrier plate includes guide slots, pivot supports, or bearing interfaces configured to maintain synchronized motion of the planet subassemblies during ratio changes. The control system may further include mechanical, hydraulic, electromechanical, or electronic actuation elements arranged to adjust the skew cam position in response to driver demand, operating conditions, or closed-loop control signals. The disclosed arrangement enables compact packaging, reduced hysteresis, improved feedback response, and precise ratio control in toroidal, traction, or other CVT architectures.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the disclosed CVT invention in a broad technical paragraph, focusing on components, subassemblies, control interfaces, and methods for changing transmission ratio.
counterfactuals.output: The disclosed continuously variable transmission (CVT) generally comprises an input drive member coupled to a prime mover, an output drive member coupled to a driven load, and a variable-ratio power-transfer assembly arranged between them, such as opposed adjustable sheaves with a belt or chain, toroidal traction elements, rollers, cones, or other variable effective-radius transmission members. The transmission includes subassemblies for supporting and positioning the ratio-varying elements, including shafts, bearings, movable pulley halves or traction members, actuators, biasing members, hydraulic circuits, lubrication passages, and housing structures. A control system interfaces with the CVT through mechanical, hydraulic, electrohydraulic, or electromechanical controls and may receive inputs such as engine speed, output speed, throttle or torque demand, vehicle speed, load, temperature, and operator commands. Ratio change is achieved by selectively changing the effective driving and driven radii or traction contact positions within the variator, for example by axially shifting pulley sheaves to alter belt pitch radius, moving traction rollers between input and output discs, or otherwise repositioning variable-contact elements. The control system commands actuators or pressure-control devices to coordinate clamping force, torque capacity, and ratio position, allowing the transmission to smoothly vary between low and high ratios, maintain a target engine or input speed, respond to acceleration or load changes, and optionally provide fixed-ratio, manual, or automatic operating modes.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract for a patent application about continuously variable transmission ratio control using a control reference nut, feedback cam, skew cam, neutralizer assembly, shift cam, and traction sun.
counterfactuals.output: A continuously variable transmission ratio control system is provided for regulating the operating ratio of a traction transmission. The system includes a control reference nut movable in response to an operator or actuator command, a feedback cam responsive to actual transmission ratio, and a skew cam arranged to generate a ratio-changing control input as a function of the difference between commanded and actual ratio positions. A neutralizer assembly cooperates with the skew cam to reduce or cancel the ratio-changing input when the commanded ratio is attained, thereby stabilizing transmission operation. A shift cam transmits the resulting control motion to adjust the angular or positional relationship of traction elements, including a traction sun, to vary the effective transmission ratio. The interaction of the control reference nut, feedback cam, skew cam, neutralizer assembly, shift cam, and traction sun provides closed-loop mechanical ratio control, enabling smooth continuously variable ratio adjustment, automatic feedback correction, and maintenance of a selected ratio without requiring continuous external actuation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise invention summary for a CVT system where carrier plates interact with skew cams and planet subassembly legs to enable shifting and ratio control.
counterfactuals.output:
An improved continuously variable transmission (CVT) system includes one or more carrier plates configured to cooperate with skew cams and planet subassembly legs to provide controlled shifting and transmission ratio adjustment. The carrier plates support and guide the planet subassemblies while the skew cams selectively impose angular or positional displacement on the planet legs. Interaction between the skew cam profiles and the planet subassembly legs causes coordinated movement of the planets relative to the carrier, thereby changing the effective operating geometry of the variator and adjusting the speed ratio.

The system enables smooth ratio control by translating cam actuation into precise displacement of the planet assemblies. The carrier plates may maintain alignment, distribute loads, and constrain motion of the planet legs during shifting, improving stability and repeatability. By using skew cams to drive the planet subassemblies through the carrier plate arrangement, the CVT can achieve compact packaging, responsive shifting behavior, and controlled ratio variation across an operating range.
